cues.en: Mike: So continuing our discussion of the ANOVA, an introduction to the ANOVA, I'm going to talk about more terminology in this video
cues.zh: Mike：繼續介紹 ANOVA。這支影片會談更多術語，

cues.en: and also some of the key assumptions underlying the ANOVA.
cues.zh: 以及 ANOVA 背後的一些重要假設。

cues.en: So let us begin.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: Here's the first important terminology, is the something-way ANOVA.
cues.zh: 第一個重要術語，是「幾因子 ANOVA」。

cues.en: The number here is just the number of factors.
cues.zh: 這裡的數字只表示因子的數量。

cues.en: So for example, we say a one-way ANOVA means that there is just one factor.
cues.zh: 例如，單因子 ANOVA 表示只有一個因子。

cues.en: Now that doesn't restrict or tell us about the number of levels within that factor.
cues.zh: 並沒有規定，也沒有告訴我們因子裡有幾個水準。

cues.en: It just tells us how many factors there are.
cues.zh: 只告訴我們因子有幾個。

cues.en: So here's an example of an experiment that would be analyzed with a one-way ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這是一個適合用單因子 ANOVA 分析的實驗例子。

cues.en: Determine the influence of day of week on iPhone purchases.
cues.zh: 判定一週中的星期幾，對 iPhone 購買量的影響。

cues.en: So there's only one factor here, and how many levels are there in this factor?
cues.zh: 這裡只有一個因子，這個因子有幾個水準？

cues.en: Right, there's seven factors because there are seven days of the week.
cues.zh: 對，有七個因子，因為一週有七天。

cues.en: We could also simplify this.
cues.zh: 也可以簡化。

cues.en: If you wanna make this two levels, maybe you want to say like, you know, during the week, so Monday to Friday, versus weekend, Saturday, Sunday.
cues.zh: 如果想改成兩個水準，可以分成平日，也就是週一到週五，以及週末，週六與週日。

cues.en: But we can think of this as a seven-level one-factor ANOVA.
cues.zh: 不過這裡可以把它看成七個水準、單一因子的 ANOVA。

cues.en: Okay, so that's a one-way ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這就是單因子 ANOVA。

cues.en: A two-way ANOVA is just an ANOVA where we have two factors.
cues.zh: 雙因子 ANOVA，就是有兩個因子的 ANOVA。

cues.en: So here, an example would be building on this.
cues.zh: 可以在這個例子上擴充。

cues.en: Determine the influences of day of week and gender on iPhone purchases.
cues.zh: 判定星期幾與性別，對 iPhone 購買量的影響。

cues.en: So now we have day of week, which is one factor and seven levels, and then we have gender, which is the other factor, and this one has two levels.
cues.zh: 星期幾是一個因子，有七個水準；性別是另一個因子，這裡有兩個水準。

cues.en: And I don't know, maybe men purchase iPhones more during the week and women more on the weekend.
cues.zh: 我也不知道，也許男性比較常在平日買 iPhone，女性比較常在週末買。

cues.en: I don't know where I come up with these examples.
cues.zh: 不知道我怎麼會想到這些例子。

cues.en: Anyway, so the blank-way ANOVA is just referring to the number of factors in the ANOVA.
cues.zh: 總之，幾因子 ANOVA，只是在說 ANOVA 的因子數量。

cues.en: Okay, so then we have a repeated-measures ANOVA and a repeated-measures ANOVA basically just means that we are taking multiple measurements
cues.zh: 接著是重複量測 ANOVA，基本上表示對同一批個體，進行多次量測，

cues.en: from the same individuals, so if at least one factor involves multiple measurements from the same individual.
cues.zh: 也就是至少一個因子，涉及同一個體的多次量測。

cues.en: Here's an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: We want to determine the effects of snack type on mood.
cues.zh: 想判定點心種類對心情的影響。

cues.en: So here's what we do.
cues.zh: 方法如下。

cues.en: We get a bunch of volunteers and we force them to eat chocolate for two days, and then they eat potato chips for two days, and then they eat ice cream for two days,
cues.zh: 找來一群志願者，強迫他們吃兩天巧克力，再吃兩天洋芋片，再吃兩天冰淇淋，

cues.en: and obviously, the order should be randomized here.
cues.zh: 順序當然應該隨機化。

cues.en: Now this sounds like a really great experiment.
cues.zh: 聽起來是很棒的實驗。

cues.en: You know, where can we sign up to volunteer to participate in this experiment?
cues.zh: 要去哪裡報名當志願者，參加這個實驗呢？

cues.en: But the point is, so we have the same individuals, the same volunteers are participating in all three of these levels within the factor.
cues.zh: 重點是，同一批志願者參與了這個因子內全部三個水準。

cues.en: So this is a one-way ANOVA, because we're just looking at one factor, which is snack type.
cues.zh: 這是單因子 ANOVA，因為只研究一個因子，也就是點心種類。

cues.en: There's three levels, chocolate, potato chips, and ice cream, the dependent variable is mood, and it's repeated measures because each individual person,
cues.zh: 三個水準是巧克力、洋芋片與冰淇淋；依變數是心情。它是重複量測，因為每個人，

cues.en: each participant in our experiment is going to participate in all of the levels of this factor, so we get repeated measures from each individual.
cues.zh: 也就是實驗中的每位參與者，都會參與這個因子的所有水準，因此每個人都提供重複量測。

cues.en: Okay, so then we have another term called balanced versus unbalanced ANOVA.
cues.zh: 接著是另一個術語，平衡與不平衡 ANOVA。

cues.en: And a balanced ANOVA means that there's the same number of data points in each cell, and an unbalanced ANOVA means that there are different number of data points in different cells.
cues.zh: 平衡 ANOVA 表示每個格子的資料點數量相同；不平衡 ANOVA 則表示不同格子的資料點數量不同。

cues.en: So here we see the table of factors and levels from the example in the previous video.
cues.zh: 這裡是上一支影片例子的因子與水準表。

cues.en: So notice here, this number here refers to the number of individuals in each of these groups, so this means that in total,
cues.zh: 注意，這裡的數字表示各組人數，因此整個實驗總共有

cues.en: we have 120 participants in our experiment.
cues.zh: 120 位參與者。

cues.en: There's 20 of these participants are younger and they're getting medication A, 20 are older and getting medication A, and so on.
cues.zh: 其中 20 位較年輕、接受藥物 A，20 位較年長、接受藥物 A，依此類推。

cues.en: So this isn't repeated measurements, but every cell in this table has the same N, the same number of participants, so this is called a balanced ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這不是重複量測，但每個格子的 N、參與者數量相同，所以稱為平衡 ANOVA。

cues.en: This would be an example of an unbalanced ANOVA, and unbalanced ANOVAs can happen often, partly just by chance because of data collection.
cues.zh: 這是不平衡 ANOVA 的例子，資料收集時可能只是偶然，就經常出現不平衡。

cues.en: Sometimes it happens by cleaning.
cues.zh: 有時是清理資料造成的。

cues.en: Maybe the data were corrupted, something happened with the data, so we had to throw out some datasets.
cues.zh: 也許資料損壞，發生某些問題，所以必須丟棄部分資料集。

cues.en: Maybe one of these participants died.
cues.zh: 也許某位參與者過世。

cues.en: Unfortunately, that can happen in medical research.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，醫學研究確實可能發生這種情況。

cues.en: So there's many examples why you can have different sample sizes in different cells, but we need to know whether an ANOVA is balanced or unbalanced
cues.zh: 不同格子有不同樣本數的原因很多，但需要知道 ANOVA 是平衡還是不平衡，

cues.en: because the formulas change slightly.
cues.zh: 因為公式會有些差異。

cues.en: So essentially we can use some simplified formulas for a balanced ANOVA, and the formulas get to be a little bit trickier for unbalanced ANOVA,
cues.zh: 基本上，平衡 ANOVA 可以用較簡單的公式，不平衡 ANOVA 的公式則稍微複雜，

cues.en: just because the way that we have to cut up the variance is going to be different for different groups with different sample sizes.
cues.zh: 因為不同組別的樣本數不同，分割變異的方式也會不同。

cues.en: Alright, so then there's another term that you need to know for ANOVAs, and that is called dummy-coding.
cues.zh: 另一個 ANOVA 術語，是虛擬編碼。

cues.en: Now, you might think that this is what happens when you give unmotivated undergraduate students the job of manually keying in a bunch of data,
cues.zh: 你可能以為，這是把手動輸入大量資料的工作，交給沒幹勁的大學生時，會發生的事情，

cues.en: but that's actually not what dummy-coding refers to.
cues.zh: 但虛擬編碼不是這個意思。

cues.en: I don't know who invented this term or what they were thinking when they came up with this thing, but dummy-coding just means converting categorical variables into numbers.
cues.zh: 不知道誰發明這個詞，當時在想什麼，但虛擬編碼只是把類別變數轉成數字。

cues.en: And so it's best applied to cases with two cases, and then you often use the numbers zero and one.
cues.zh: 最適用於有兩種類別的情況，通常用 0 與 1。

cues.en: So for example, or actually, I'll show you the way that this is said first.
cues.zh: 舉例來說，或者先示範這種說法。

cues.en: So gender was entered into the ANOVA as a dummy-coded variable.
cues.zh: 性別以虛擬編碼變數的形式，納入 ANOVA。

cues.en: So gender is a categorical variable, and we're not gonna get into any political discussions here, but it's a categorical binary variable
cues.zh: 性別是類別變數，這裡不討論政治議題，在這個例子中它是二元類別變數，

cues.en: and it's entered into the ANOVA as a dummy-coded variable.
cues.zh: 以虛擬編碼變數的形式納入 ANOVA。

cues.en: So we convert the label male and female to the number zero and one, so then the way that you would interpret this factor
cues.zh: 把男性與女性的標籤，轉換成數字 0 與 1，因此解讀 ANOVA 中這個因子時，

cues.en: in the ANOVA is that the effect of the factor shows the change for the one variable compared to the zero variable.
cues.zh: 因子效果表示編碼為 1 的變數，相較於編碼為 0 的變數之變化。

cues.en: So it's like zero becomes our baseline, and what the ANOVA tells us is how the dependent variable changes
cues.zh: 0 就成為基準，而 ANOVA 告訴我們，依變數對於

cues.en: for whatever level is labeled as one.
cues.zh: 標為 1 的那個水準，如何改變。

cues.en: So here's an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Let's say we want to study lipstick usage, I don't know, so we could have a main effect of gender on lipstick use, and the way that we would interpret this,
cues.zh: 假設研究口紅使用，不知道為什麼。我們可能發現性別對口紅使用有主效應，解讀方式是，

cues.en: if gender is dummy-coded, as you see here, that whatever result we get would be positive.
cues.zh: 若性別如這裡以虛擬編碼表示，那麼得到的結果會是正的。

cues.en: So it would be for females versus males, so a positive effect would indicate that women use lipstick more than men, and then men are kind of acting like the baseline
cues.zh: 它表示女性相對於男性。正效果表示女性比男性更常使用口紅，而男性成為基準，

cues.en: against which we understand changes in females.
cues.zh: 據此理解女性的變化。

cues.en: Now the dummy-coding here is arbitrary.
cues.zh: 這裡的虛擬編碼是任意的。

cues.en: It doesn't change the statistics, it doesn't change the P-value, it doesn't change the overall model.
cues.zh: 不會改變統計結果、P 值或整體模型。

cues.en: It does, however, slightly change the interpretation.
cues.zh: 但會稍微改變解讀方式。

cues.en: So we could say that we dummy-code this to be females equal zero and males equal one, and then the exact same experiment, the exact same data,
cues.zh: 也可以把女性編為 0，男性編為 1。同樣的實驗、同樣的資料，

cues.en: our interpretation would be men used lipstick less than women.
cues.zh: 解讀就變成男性比女性更少使用口紅。

cues.en: So you can see it's the same finding, but when we dummy-code the males to be zero, then we say women use lipstick more.
cues.zh: 這是同一個發現；男性編為 0 時，說女性用得更多。

cues.en: If we dummy-code the females to be zero, then we say men use lipstick less than females.
cues.zh: 女性編為 0 時，則說男性比女性用得更少。

cues.en: So then we have an ANOVA versus a MANOVA, and ANOVA just refers to one dependent variable.
cues.zh: 接著比較 ANOVA 與 MANOVA。ANOVA 只有一個依變數。

cues.en: You can have as many independent variables as are appropriate, but there's only one dependent variable, and that's like all of the examples that I've been giving so far.
cues.zh: 自變數可以有任何適當數量，但依變數只有一個，目前舉的例子都是如此。

cues.en: Then there's a variant of the ANOVA called the MANOVA, or the M is for multivariate, so we have a multivariate ANOVA,
cues.zh: ANOVA 有個變體稱為 MANOVA，M 代表多變量，也就是多變量變異數分析，

cues.en: and this means that we can have many independent variables, but we can also have multiple dependent variables.
cues.zh: 表示可以有許多自變數，也可以有多個依變數。

cues.en: So an example would be effect of medication type on age group, like what the example was from the previous video, except now we are not only investigating
cues.zh: 例如藥物類型對年齡組別的效果，就像上一支影片的例子，只是現在不僅研究

cues.en: the disease severity, but also the total medical expenses.
cues.zh: 疾病嚴重程度，也研究總醫療費用。

cues.en: So now we have two dependent variables, the symptom, severity, and medical expenses.
cues.zh: 現在就有症狀嚴重程度與醫療費用兩個依變數。

cues.en: So this would be an example of a MANOVA.
cues.zh: 這就是 MANOVA 的例子。

cues.en: The final set of terms that I'm going to introduce you to here before getting to the assumptions of the ANOVA are fixed versus random effects.
cues.zh: 在談 ANOVA 假設之前，最後介紹一組術語：固定效應與隨機效應。

cues.en: So a fixed effects means that the number of levels in a factor is fixed out there in the world, or at least some reasonable degree.
cues.zh: 固定效應表示，因子中的水準數，在現實世界中是固定的，至少大致固定。

cues.en: So let's imagine we have a factor that is called home type.
cues.zh: 假設有一個因子，叫作居住類型。

cues.en: So there isn't like an infinite number of different home types.
cues.zh: 居住類型並不是無限多種。

cues.en: You could live in a dorm room, you could live in an apartment, you could live in a house.
cues.zh: 可以住宿舍、公寓，或獨棟住宅。

cues.en: You know, maybe we can come up with a couple of other levels for home type, but it's not that there is, you know, that we could just draw any home type at random.
cues.zh: 也許還能想出幾種其他水準，但並不是可以任意隨機抽出無窮種類的居住類型。

cues.en: There's a fixed number of home types.
cues.zh: 居住類型的數量固定。

cues.en: Another example would be, let's say we're looking at a factor of operating system.
cues.zh: 另一個例子，是作業系統因子。

cues.en: So there's basically just three operating systems that we have.
cues.zh: 基本上只有三種作業系統。

cues.en: There's Windows, there's Mac, and there's Linux, so there isn't like some infinite number of possible operating systems.
cues.zh: Windows、Mac 與 Linux，不是有無限多種可能作業系統。

cues.en: We only have three possible levels, so that would be a fixed factor.
cues.zh: 只有三個可能的水準，所以是固定因子。

cues.en: And then we have random effects, and this means that the levels of the factor are random or continuous in the population.
cues.zh: 隨機效應則表示，因子的水準在母體中是隨機或連續的。

cues.en: Now, random is not the same thing as continuous.
cues.zh: 隨機與連續並不是同一件事。

cues.en: Let me give you two examples.
cues.zh: 舉兩個例子。

cues.en: So we have age, salary, and here I'm saying nurse.
cues.zh: 有年齡、薪資，以及這裡寫的護理師。

cues.en: So age would be a random factor because it is continuous.
cues.zh: 年齡會是隨機因子，因為它是連續的。

cues.en: Now we could discretize age, like I showed in the previous video, where we had the example of older people and younger people.
cues.zh: 當然也可以離散化年齡，就像上一支影片分成年長者與年輕人的例子。

cues.en: So we just say arbitrarily that 50 years old is the threshold, and we binarize age, but otherwise, age is going to be a random factor.
cues.zh: 任意把 50 歲設為門檻，將年齡二元化；否則年齡會是隨機因子。

cues.en: Salary is also a random factor, and here I write the word nurse, but this could be an individual.
cues.zh: 薪資也是隨機因子。這裡寫護理師，但也可以是個體。

cues.en: This is just a reminder for me to give you a specific example.
cues.zh: 這只是提醒自己，要舉一個具體例子。

cues.en: So let's say we're doing a study about how well patients recover depending on their intake process.
cues.zh: 假設研究患者的恢復情況，如何取決於入院接待流程。

cues.en: So you have an intake nurse.
cues.zh: 有一位入院接待護理師。

cues.en: That would be the nurse that you first speak with when you go into the hospital.
cues.zh: 就是進醫院時，首先與你交談的護理師。

cues.en: Now, not all nurses are the same.
cues.zh: 並非所有護理師都相同。

cues.en: Some nurses are a little bit more personable, some nurses are a little bit more empathetic, some nurses are a little bit more let's say cold and efficient,
cues.zh: 有些更親切，有些更有同理心，有些則可能比較冷淡、講求效率，

cues.en: and just sort of they're doing their job.
cues.zh: 只是在做自己的工作。

cues.en: So there's a variety of different types of nurses.
cues.zh: 所以有各種不同類型的護理師。

cues.en: They're random factors.
cues.zh: 它們是隨機因子。

cues.en: So if we pick, let's say four nurses at random, and those four nurses are the different levels in our factor of intake nurse,
cues.zh: 假設隨機選四位護理師，作為入院接待護理師因子的四個水準，

cues.en: then if we find an effect of nurse, so that factor ends up being significant in the ANOVA, then we know that there are individual differences in the nurses in this random factor
cues.zh: 如果發現護理師有效果，也就是這個因子在 ANOVA 中顯著，就知道這個隨機因子中的護理師個體差異，

cues.en: that are important for later recovery.
cues.zh: 對後續恢復很重要。

cues.en: Again, I'm just making up that example.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，例子只是我編的。

cues.en: I don't know if that actually would be a significant effect.
cues.zh: 不知道實際上是否會有顯著效果。

cues.en: Okay, so a fixed effects ANOVA means that all of the factors are fixed.
cues.zh: 固定效應 ANOVA，表示所有因子都是固定的。

cues.en: A random effects ANOVA means that all of the factors are random, and a mixed effects ANOVA is, you guessed it, referring to an ANOVA where some of the factors are fixed,
cues.zh: 隨機效應 ANOVA，表示所有因子都是隨機的；混合效應 ANOVA，顧名思義，表示部分因子固定，

cues.en: so at least one factor is fixed, and at least one factor is random.
cues.zh: 也就是至少一個固定因子，以及至少一個隨機因子。

cues.en: Okay, so here's just a quick summary and then I'm gonna give you two examples.
cues.zh: 這裡快速整理，再舉兩個例子。

cues.en: So this is an example of a mixed effects ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這是一個混合效應 ANOVA 的例子。

cues.en: We want to determine, so we're doing some research on happiness.
cues.zh: 假設研究幸福感。

cues.en: So we determine whether subjective happiness, which just means you ask people, "How happy do you think you are?"
cues.zh: 量測主觀幸福感，也就是詢問：「你認為自己有多幸福？」

cues.en: And we wanna know whether that's influenced by their home type and by their age.
cues.zh: 想知道它是否受居住類型與年齡影響。

cues.en: So home type, as I mentioned a moment ago, I'm considering to be a fixed effect.
cues.zh: 如剛才提到，這裡把居住類型視為固定效應。

cues.en: There aren't that many home types that are available.
cues.zh: 可選的居住類型並不多。

cues.en: So you could imagine all sorts of possibilities.
cues.zh: 可以想像各種可能性。

cues.en: Maybe people who live in a home are happier because they have more space.
cues.zh: 也許住獨棟住宅的人更幸福，因為空間更多。

cues.en: Maybe people who live in apartments are happier because they're closer to other people.
cues.zh: 也許住公寓的人更幸福，因為離其他人更近。

cues.en: They feel like they're in a community, I don't know.
cues.zh: 有社群歸屬感，我也不知道。

cues.en: And age would be a random factor.
cues.zh: 年齡則是隨機因子。

cues.en: And an example of when age would not be a significant effect is, you know, let's say people are generally happy throughout their entire life.
cues.zh: 年齡效果不顯著的例子，是人們一生中大致都很幸福。

cues.en: So subjective happiness stays roughly the same for all ages.
cues.zh: 各年齡的主觀幸福感大致相同。

cues.en: So that would be an example of where we have a random factor, but it is not significant.
cues.zh: 這就是有隨機因子，但效果不顯著的例子。

cues.en: Okay, so here's another example.
cues.zh: 再舉一個例子。

cues.en: Let's say, yeah, we're doing some medical research on the effects of medication.
cues.zh: 假設進行藥物效果的醫學研究。

cues.en: Again, we have three different types of medication, let's say two real medications and a placebo, but then we have different experimenters who are giving the medication to the patients.
cues.zh: 同樣有三種藥物，例如兩種真藥與安慰劑，但由不同實驗人員把藥給患者。

cues.en: And again, some of these experimenters are going to be very nice, very simpatico, very pleasant to be around, and other experimenters might be kind of old and grumpy
cues.zh: 有些實驗人員很友善、親切、讓人相處愉快，另一些可能年紀大、脾氣差，

cues.en: and they don't care about the research.
cues.zh: 也不關心研究。

cues.en: They're just doing it because someone made them do it.
cues.zh: 只是因為有人叫他們做，才在做。

cues.en: So maybe there's something about the experimenter that influences the effects of the medication.
cues.zh: 所以，實驗人員的某些特質，可能影響藥物效果。

cues.en: So the experimenter is a random factor, and the medication type is a fixed factor.
cues.zh: 實驗人員是隨機因子，藥物類型是固定因子。

cues.en: One of the reasons why ANOVAs are so popular and so widely used is that they're pretty robust.
cues.zh: ANOVA 這麼受歡迎、使用這麼廣泛，其中一個原因是相當穩健。

cues.en: They work pretty well, even for violations of the assumptions of the ANOVA.
cues.zh: 即使違反 ANOVA 的假設，表現仍然不錯。

cues.en: Nonetheless, there are some important assumptions of ANOVAs, and if your data really strongly violate these assumptions, then you might have to think about
cues.zh: 但 ANOVA 還是有些重要假設，如果資料嚴重違反，可能必須考慮

cues.en: either doing something with the data to clean the data or transform the data or applying a nonparametric ANOVA.
cues.zh: 清理資料、轉換資料，或使用無母數 ANOVA。

cues.en: So one example, or one of the assumptions of ANOVA is independence.
cues.zh: 其中一個假設是獨立性。

cues.en: So this means that the data are sampled independently of each other in the population to which you want to generalize.
cues.zh: 表示資料從想要推論的母體中，彼此獨立地抽樣。

cues.en: So when we're doing this medical research on the effects of medication on COVID-19, then we want to make sure that we're getting independently sampled patients,
cues.zh: 研究藥物對 COVID-19 的效果時，要確保患者是獨立抽樣，

cues.en: instead of there being some kind of a relationship between the patients.
cues.zh: 而不是彼此有某種關係。

cues.en: So for example, let's say we only take patients who are in the same family, you know, so one person gets the virus and brings it home,
cues.zh: 例如，只選同一家庭的患者，一個人感染病毒帶回家，

cues.en: and they live in a big house with 10 people, and all 10 of them get sick, so now we want to test all 10 of those people.
cues.zh: 住在有 10 個人的大家庭，10 個人全生病，於是想測試全部 10 人。

cues.en: Well, that's not a very good sample.
cues.zh: 這就不是很好的樣本。

cues.en: The data are not sampled independently, and maybe that's going to screw up the experiment and the generalization, because it turns out that that one specific family
cues.zh: 資料不是獨立抽樣，可能影響實驗與推論，因為這個特定家庭

cues.en: has a particular genetic background that makes them be affected by the drug in a way that isn't representative of the population.
cues.zh: 有特殊遺傳背景，讓藥物對他們的影響不具母體代表性。

cues.en: Okay, so the data for an ANOVA should all be randomly sampled.
cues.zh: 所以 ANOVA 資料都應該隨機抽樣。

cues.en: And then we have the assumption of normality, which basically means that the data are drawn from a population that has a normal distribution or a Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 還有常態性假設，基本上表示資料來自常態或高斯分布的母體。

cues.en: And it's often interpreted as saying that the residuals, which is the unexplained variance after fitting the model, are normally or Gaussian distributed.
cues.zh: 常解讀為殘差，也就是模型擬合後尚未解釋的變異，服從常態或高斯分布。

cues.en: So this means that the model isn't biased in any specific way towards some data points, against other data points.
cues.zh: 表示模型不會以某種特定方式偏向某些資料點，而不利於其他點。

cues.en: And then we have another assumption, which is called homogeneity of variance, and it's also, it's related to this term called heteroscedasticity,
cues.zh: 另一個假設是變異數同質性，也與 heteroscedasticity 這個詞有關，

cues.en: which is hands-down my most favoritest word in all of statistics to say, heteroscedasticity.
cues.zh: 這絕對是整個統計學中，我最喜歡念的字：heteroscedasticity。

cues.en: It's really fun to say, and if you're not a native English speaker, you might need to practice this several times before you can get it right, but it really rolls off the tongue, heteroscedasticity
cues.zh: 念起來非常有趣，如果不是英語母語者，可能需要練習幾次才能念對，不過真的很順口：heteroscedasticity。

cues.en: So if you'd like to pause the video and just practice saying that word, then I encourage that, I support that.
cues.zh: 如果想暫停影片練習念這個詞，我鼓勵，也支持。

cues.en: Okay, but what does this mean?
cues.zh: 那它是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, heteroscedasticity is actually the opposite of homogeneity of variance.
cues.zh: heteroscedasticity，也就是異質變異性，其實與變異數同質性相反。

cues.en: It means that the variance, or homogeneity of variance means that the variance and in the different cells and the different levels and the different factors are roughly the same.
cues.zh: 變異數同質性表示，不同格子、不同水準與不同因子中的變異數，大致相同。

cues.en: So they don't need to be exactly identical, but if some of your ANOVA cells, so some of your combinations of levels and factors are much, much more variable,
cues.zh: 不需要完全一致，但如果某些 ANOVA 格子，也就是某些因子與水準組合，變動大得多，

cues.en: and other cells are much, much less variable, then that can be a problem for the ANOVA.
cues.zh: 另一些格子的變動卻小得多，就可能對 ANOVA 造成問題。

cues.en: The reason why that can be a problem is that the ANOVA, the way the ANOVA works, is all about dividing up the total amount of variance in the data,
cues.zh: 原因是 ANOVA 的運作，完全圍繞把資料中的總變異，

cues.en: according to different factors and different levels of the factor.
cues.zh: 依據不同因子與因子水準分割。

cues.en: So if you naturally start off with way different variance in different parts of the data space, then that's going to introduce a bias
cues.zh: 如果一開始，資料空間不同部分的變異就差很多，便會在

cues.en: into the ANOVA estimation.
cues.zh: ANOVA 估計中引入偏差。

cues.en: Okay, so as I mentioned, ANOVAs are fairly robust to minor to kind of moderate-ish violations of the assumption.
cues.zh: 如前所述，對輕微到中度的假設違反，ANOVA 相當穩健。

cues.en: This independence assumption is really important for generalizing to a larger population.
cues.zh: 獨立性假設對推論到更大母體非常重要。

cues.en: If your data are not exactly normally distributed and the variance is not exactly the same across the different cells, that's probably not a big deal, as long as it isn't, you know, too bad.
cues.zh: 如果資料不完全常態，各格子的變異數也不完全相同，只要不太嚴重，可能不是大問題。

cues.en: It can be difficult to say exactly what level of violation is really detrimental.
cues.zh: 很難明確說，違反到什麼程度，才真的有害。

cues.en: But if these assumptions are definitely not met, then there is some alternatives to the parametric ANOVA,
cues.zh: 但如果確實不符合假設，參數 ANOVA 還有替代方案，

cues.en: which is the nonparametric ANOVA, and the main one there is called the Kruskal-Wallis test, and that only works for the one-way ANOVA,
cues.zh: 也就是無母數 ANOVA，其中主要方法叫 Kruskal–Wallis 檢定，只適用於單因子 ANOVA，

cues.en: and it works by looking at the rank-transformed data instead of the data in their original scale.
cues.zh: 使用秩轉換後的資料，而不是原始尺度的資料。

cues.en: Now, the thing is that nonparametric ANOVAs are quite infrequently used.
cues.zh: 不過，無母數 ANOVA 使用頻率相當低。

cues.en: They're not that often used, and so when people see that you're using a nonparametric ANOVA, I don't know, some people don't react to that very well,
cues.zh: 並不常用，所以當有人看到你用無母數 ANOVA，有些人的反應可能不太好，

cues.en: and it might end up just causing more headaches than what you really get out of it.
cues.zh: 最後帶來的麻煩，可能超過實際收穫。

cues.en: So whenever possible, try to get your data to be in a state where it's appropriate to use a parametric ANOVA.
cues.zh: 因此，只要可能，就試著讓資料處於適合參數 ANOVA 的狀態。

cues.en: So in this video, I provided the second part of the introduction to the ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這支影片是 ANOVA 入門的第二部分。

cues.en: I went over a lot of different terminologies, and I talked about some of the assumptions underlying the ANOVAs.
cues.zh: 介紹了許多術語，也討論 ANOVA 背後的一些假設。

cues.en: Now you are ready to start learning the math of how the ANOVA really works.
cues.zh: 現在你已準備好，開始學習 ANOVA 真正運作的數學。
